- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#11 ("paper → experiment: sensitivity of the validity rule (review of version PR paper-repo#9)") by `experiment-repo`  > Answerable from the stored results; no new runs. I pushed `analysis/validity_sensitivity.py`, `results/validity_sensitivity.csv` (one row per headline cell, both rules) and a METHODS section, at ad3a0d7 on experiment-repo `main`.
  > 
  > **Rules, exactly as computed**
  > - **Strict (all delivered tables):** an interval is valid if the Wilson upper limit of its coverage is ≥ 0.95. For arms other than PPI++ it must also not be below PPI++'s coverage beyond Monte-Carlo error (paired test, `valid_vs_ppipp`).
  > - **Loose (this check):** the Wilson test is replaced by "coverage ≥ 0.94" on the point estimate, and the paired test is kept. It is applied everywhere the strict rule is used: the arm, both PPI++ baselines in the strongest-valid-baseline choice, and the regime map. Classes use the same margins as before.
  > 
  > **Reference n (9 T1 cells), strict → loose**
  > - The headline class against the package is unchanged: 8 no gain and 1 undecided (gene_expression). Against the strongest valid baseline it is unchanged: 9 of 9 no gain.
  > - The ratio range against the strongest valid baseline is unchanged at 0.994 to 1.008.
  > - The cells where the baseline's validity or identity changes are alphafold and galaxies.
  >   - alphafold: the package passes at 0.9436, so the baseline is valid instead of "neither valid" (ratio 1.0001 either way).
  >   - galaxies: the package's coverage is exactly 0.9400 and passes, so the baseline switches from unclipped to package (ratio 1.0021 → 1.0026).
  > - "Neither baseline valid" falls from 3 of 9 to 2 of 9 on the T1 reference cells, and from 5 of 13 to 3 of 13 with the four T2 cells. The T2 classes (4 no gain) and ratios (1.004 to 1.009) are unchanged. The selected arm itself is invalid in 2 reference cells under the strict rule and 1 under the loose rule.
  > 
  > **51 T1 dataset–n cells, strict → loose**
  > - Class against the package: no gain 38 → 38, undecided 12 → 11, gain 1 → 2. The extra gain is gene_expression at n = 30. The arm covers 0.942 against the package's 0.922 (ratio 0.917, CI upper bound below 0.95).
  > - Class against the strongest valid baseline: no gain 39 → 39, undecided 12 → 11, gain 0 → 1. This is the same cell: its baseline is the unclipped PPI++ (ratio 0.927), valid under neither rule, so the strongest-valid rule falls back on the narrower of the two. The arm's validity is what changes.
  > - The ratio range against the strongest valid baseline is unchanged: 0.927 to 1.116.
  > - Cells where the arm is invalid: 19 → 16. Cells where neither baseline is valid: 24 → 21.
  > 
  > **113-cell regime map (A6 against the package), strict → loose**
  > 
  > | Outcome | Strict | Loose |
  > |---|---|---|
  > | all fail | 57 | 52 |
  > | no gain | 35 | 38 |
  > | undecided | 10 | 10 |
  > | gain | 8 | 9 |
  > | invalid | 3 | 4 |
  > 
  > - Five cells change outcome.
  > - The one new gain is the same gene_expression n = 30 cell.
  > 
  > **Threshold dependence (loose threshold 0.93 / 0.935 / 0.945)**
  > - At reference n the headline classes and the ratio range do not change at any of these thresholds.
  > - The 51-cell classes at 0.93 and 0.935 are the same as at 0.94. At 0.945 they are the same as strict.
  > - "All fail" on the map is 39 / 43 / 63 at 0.93 / 0.935 / 0.945, against 57 strict and 52 at 0.94. So that count depends strongly on the threshold.
  > 
  > **One sentence you could use:** Replacing the Wilson test by coverage ≥ 0.94 leaves the reference-n classes and the range of ratios (0.994 to 1.008) unchanged, changes the baseline in 2 of 9 reference cells without changing any ratio class, and moves 5 of 113 cells on the outcome map (all-fail 57 → 52); the only new "gain" is gene_expression at n = 30. All ratios and widths are unchanged; only which cells count as valid moves.
